_comment: Draft fragment for alignment-performance.json (contract 1.1.0). Merge tools/datasets/metrics/resources/figures/reach/artifacts/caveats; methods is a paragraph to add. Pareto figures are built with contract.pareto_figure on the 'pooled' resources (per 100M pairs).
methods: Exact versus pseudo-alignment. Singlet aligns every read to the genome with a STAR fork and counts from the alignments (pileup); alevin-fry (via simpleaf and piscem) maps reads by k-mer matching to a splici index of the annotated transcripts and introns. The genome-wide aligner costs more CPU and memory and places reads outside the annotation; the pseudoaligner is several times faster. This fragment measures both sides on real data. Truth: (1) species of origin in a human-mouse barnyard (hgmm1k_v3); (2) no chrY in female-derived HEK293T cells; (3) CITE-seq protein against RNA on the same PBMC cells. No simulated reads are used. All tools get the same FASTQs, the 10x 2024-A references, the same cells (published Cell Ranger barcodes) and, for timing, one node and 16 or 4 threads. 10x software was not run: Cell Ranger is the published 3.0.0 matrix (older references). Runtime is reported as CPU-hours per 100M read pairs with wall time secondary; Singlet includes its .1fq encode step, labelled.

tools.name: singlet
tools.params: singlet-campaign <sample>.1fq --ref-base REF --genome-dir STAR_2.7.11b_index --exons genes.gtf --out-prefix OUT/ --threads N --pipeline --output-format mtx --raw-matrix  (after `singlet encode`); counts = raw_feature_bc_matrix (exon+intron, each molecule once); exact genome-wide alignment by the STAR fork, then pileup. Encode step reported separately.

tools.name: STARsolo
tools.params: STAR --soloType CB_UMI_Simple --soloCBlen 16 --soloUMIlen 12 --soloStrand Forward --soloFeatures Gene GeneFull Velocyto --soloCellFilter EmptyDrops_CR --soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts --soloUMIfiltering MultiGeneUMI_CR --soloUMIdedup 1MM_CR --clipAdapterType CellRanger4 --outFilterScoreMin 30 --outSAMtype None; GeneFull scored (exon+intron)

tools.name: alevin-fry
tools.params: simpleaf quant --chemistry 10xv3 --expected-ori fw --resolution cr-like --unfiltered-pl 3M-february-2018.txt (splici index of the 10x 2024-A GTF, USA mode); counts = spliced+unspliced+ambiguous

tools.name: alevin-fry-em
tools.params: same mapping and permit list as alevin-fry; alevin-fry quant -r cr-like-em (EM resolution of multi-gene UMIs); quant step timed separately

tools.name: cellranger-published
tools.params: 10x Genomics PUBLISHED Cell Ranger 3.0.0 filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 (not re-run; no 10x software was installed or run). Older references than the other tools: hg19+mm10 for hgmm1k_v3, GRCh38 (3.0.0) for pbmc1k_cite_v3: https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/hgmm_1k_v3/hgmm_1k_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 ; https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/3.0.0/pbmc_1k_protein_v3/pbmc_1k_protein_v3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5. No runtime reported.

datasets.title: 10x HEK293T + NIH3T3 1:1, 1k, 3' v3 (77M read pairs)
datasets.truth: Species of origin: a cell is human or mouse (pure cells: >=90% of UMIs one species in the published Cell Ranger matrix). UMIs of the other species inside a pure cell are mapping errors or ambient RNA (identical for every tool on the same reads). Second truth: HEK293T is female-derived, so UMIs on non-PAR chrY genes in human cells are false positives.
datasets.notes: 1,046 Cell Ranger cells: 495 pure human, 544 pure mouse, 7 mixed.

datasets.title: 10x PBMC 1k + TotalSeq-B (pbmc_1k_protein_v3), 3' v3
datasets.truth: Orthogonal assay: antibody-derived tags (protein) measured on the same cells. RNA of the matching gene should rank cells like the protein.
datasets.notes: Cells = published Cell Ranger filtered barcodes; protein = Cell Ranger Antibody Capture counts, CLR-normalised.

datasets.title: 10x PBMC 1k, 3' v3 (66.6M read pairs)
datasets.truth: No per-molecule truth. Used for runtime and memory (same reads, same node, same threads) and for read accounting.
datasets.notes: Runtime dataset: 16 threads and 4 threads on one node.

metrics.name: Accuracy score: mean of each tool's value relative to the best tool

rule.rationale: 2% of the score: smaller than the bootstrap half-widths of the components (they are 5-10% relative)

Each is scaled to the best of the four runnable tools (best/value for errors, value/best for correlation); equal weights.

caveats: DRAFT, wound down early. Real truth only (no simulated reads): barnyard species, HEK293T chrY, CITE-seq protein; nothing here is simulated.

Not measured: long-read-validated spliced/unspliced, isoforms or junction truth (no matched public short+long-read 10x dataset was confirmed); spike-ins (ERCC/SIRV) were not found in the cohort. Spliced/unspliced accuracy is therefore not claimed.

One barnyard dataset (hgmm1k_v3, 495 human + 544 mouse pure cells) and one CITE-seq dataset (pbmc1k_cite_v3); the chrY truth rests on HEK293T being female-derived (published karyotype, not checked in these reads). PBMC donors are male, so chrY is not scored there.

Cross-species UMIs include ambient RNA; it is shared by all tools on the same reads, so only differences between tools are interpretable. About 15.5k of Singlet's and 13.0k of STARsolo's wrong-species UMIs sit in one 5-kb window of human LINC00486 (chr2:32.915-32.920 Mb) seen at equal rates in human and mouse cells with 2% mismatches; 90% of the mouse-cell reads do not map to the mouse genome alone. Whether those molecules are real is unresolved; alevin-fry does not count them.
Cell Ranger is 10x's PUBLISHED 3.0.0 matrix (hg19+mm10 for hgmm1k_v3; GRCh38 3.0.0 for pbmc1k_cite_v3), not re-run, and has no runtime. Its chrY value is omitted (hg19 gene ids).

Timings: one node (b002 Xeon Gold 6226, shared with other jobs), 66.6M pairs, one run per tool and thread count. Singlet includes its .1fq encode step, which the campaign runs on the 1-core download stage. The resource metrics are expected to FAIL against alevin-fry: that is the cost of exact genome-wide alignment.
Per-cell artifacts are not yet uploaded: sha256 and urls are missing, so this fragment cannot be final.
